components_that_could_ship_without_U4: None as an edition: the spec's atomicity rule (edition ships whole or not at all) forbids a partial edition. Components 2/3/6/7 (market close, SITREP digest, corrections, archive) are inputs to an edition, not shippable substitutes for one, and the market-close inputs themselves are stale (see market source gap in the full-sync report).
exact_decision_needed_from_yasin_or_dele: 1) Confirm the Tier-A definition in data terms: which stored label, if any, marks a Tier-A item — or appoint an editor to label Tier-A items explicitly per edition (an editorial selection file, as generate_nightly.py --selection expects).
2) Confirm which score, if any, is the brief score for the '>=70' brief rule — or rule that briefs are selected editorially per edition, not by score.
3) Confirm the ownrewrite candidate rule: which stored score, if any, is the ownrewrite score — or rule that ownrewrite candidates are named editorially per edition.

A single-word confirmation of the spec's PROPOSED pins is NOT sufficient on its own, because the proposed pins point at data that does not exist in the tables; the decision must name the actual source (or an explicit per-edition editorial list). Until then, nightly stays held and this verdict is re-issued by every regeneration run.
what_was_not_done: No selection file was fabricated, no edition file was written, nightly.json was not created, and the nightly manifest section was not touched (it stays honestly not_yet_published, count 0).
No existing edition was invented for any Shamsi day, and no past day was backfilled.
why_held: U4 selection criteria cannot be settled conservatively from the v4 nightly spec (docs/big-update/phases4-5-market-nightly-spec.md §5.3): the spec itself marks all three pins as SPEC DECISIONS awaiting editorial confirmation, and the implementing generator (edge/generate_nightly.py) refuses real-data selection for exactly this reason (u4_status = blocked_for_real_data without an explicit editorial selection file).

Tier-A flag: no tier_a column exists in data_core.article_extracts, data_core.items, or data_core.channel_posts (column lists verified read-only 2026-10-26). The spec's proposed pin (editorial-pass deep-analysis label in the decision log) is not present as data the generator can read.

Brief score (>=70): no brief-score field exists in any source table. The spec warns never to run two meanings of '>=70' at once: the Law-15 urgency_score belongs to typed channel items, NOT to briefs, so substituting it would be a category error, not a conservative settlement.
Ownrewrite score (>30): no ownrewrite-score field exists in any source table; the keypoints rule-score is computed at selection time and never stored, so it cannot be sourced from data.

Nightly full articles additionally require a >=60% fresh-text re-edit against the channel post body (spec §5.5, enforced by publish_edge.py: a full article without channel_post_body fails verification). No store holds channel post bodies: posted carries headlines only, and format_log carries message_id/date only. So full-article freshness is unauditable from available data; writing re-edits without the post bodies would be invented content. (Brief summaries do not need the 60% check, but brief selection itself is U4-blocked above.)
